title: VPC approval simulations and audit protocol notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This note collects results from an initial set of approval-gate simulations and proposes a lightweight audit-event protocol for customer-managed networking handoffs. The goal is to have a repeatable test harness that operators, SEs, and the control-plane team can run to validate: (1) operator approval workflows under different load/latency conditions, (2) audit event completeness for forensics, (3) SLA impact from approval delays, and (4) deterministic rollback traces for incident postmortems.

Scope (what is covered in this draft):
- Approval gating: manual operator approvals, delegated approvals (customer admin + Redwood operator), and automated policy checks (CIDR overlap, peering policies).
- Audit events: minimum required fields, sampling strategy, and retention tiering.
- Simulations: synthetic change bursts, flaky network, and conflicting change scenarios.
- Onboarding play: sequence for a new customer VPC handover including required artifacts and observable signals.

Key definitions (short):
- Approval event: any user- or system-initiated action that must be explicitly allowed to proceed by a valid actor.
- Evidence bundle: collected metadata required for attestation (config snapshot, operator identity, ticket id, cryptographic signature).
- Handover success criteria: connectivity validated for test endpoint, audit events recorded for each approval step, and forward-compatibility checks (no incompatible route tables).

Proposed audit-event protocol (minimal event fields):
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- actor_id: short string (redwood:user:ashapatel or cust:admin:acme-netops)
- actor_role: {operator, customer_admin, system}
- action: short verb (request_approval, grant_approval, revoke_approval, apply_change, rollback)
- resource: resource path (customer/123/vpc/abc/route-table)
- outcome: {allowed, denied, error}
- evidence_refs: comma-separated ids pointing to stored artifacts
- request_trace_id: correlates all events for a single change attempt

(We intentionally keep the payload flat and small so it can be forwarded to customer SIEMs and to our internal audit pipeline without schema explosion.)

Retention and sampling recommendations:
- Full-fidelity (no sampling) for approve/grant/revoke actions for 90 days in high-retention customers (enterprise tier).
- 1-in-10 sampling for routine read-only policy checks for 30 days to save cost.
- Unique per-request trace stored for 365 days for customers with compliance add-on (possible hashed redaction for PII).

Simulator harness outline (ops-sim):
- Inputs: list of planned change events, synthetic latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), actor mix percentages (80% customer, 20% Redwood), and nightly conflict injection (e.g., simultaneous route changes).
- Runner: stateless microservice that emits audit events into the same event sink as production (Kafka topic staging-audit).
- Validators: post-run checks that ensure every request_trace_id has either a final apply_change with outcome=allowed or a documented rollback with outcome=error/revoked.
- Outputs: per-run CSV with approval-latency distribution, missed-evidence-count, and policy-failure-rate.

Example simulation scenario (short):
1) 200 change requests over 10s (burst) from two customer admins.
2) Autosystems perform preliminary policy checks and queue 140 changes for automated apply. 60 require human approval.
3) We simulate a single SRE operator approving changes with 1.5s p50 latency, but network intermittency causes 5% of approvals to return timeout on apply.
4) Validator finds 3 trace_ids missing evidence_refs -> escalate as data-loss risk.

Operational acceptance criteria (for rollout):
- No more than 0.5% of approval requests should complete without a matching evidence bundle in the audit sink.
- Approval-to-apply median latency < 3s for dedicated-operator flows, < 6s for delegated flows.
- Rollback path exercised by simulator must have clear trace with at least one operator comment attached.

Onboarding checklist (customer-managed VPC handover):
- Customer provides CIDR allocation and peering prerequisites (ticket id).
- Customer signs delegated-admin contract and supplies desired operator contacts.
- We provision temporary test endpoint and run connectivity validation (ICMP/TCP/healthcheck).
- Audit: first successful apply_change must include at least 2 evidence_refs (config snapshot + operator signature).

Incident/forensics guidance (how to use these logs):
- Start from request_trace_id, enumerate events sorted by timestamp_utc, confirm actor_id and evidence_refs.
- If evidence_refs missing, check off-system storage (S3 bucket naming pattern) and fallback to archived Kafka offsets.
- If audit pipeline shows data-loss, mark impacted customers and triage per data-retention SLA.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Missing evidence bundle -> high impact, medium likelihood (mitigations: local write-ahead log, synchronous ack before apply).
- Approval race -> medium impact, high likelihood under burst -> mitigation: optimistic locking + deterministic conflict resolution rules.
- Latency spikes during operator approval -> medium impact, medium likelihood -> mitigation: allow automated soft-approve for low-risk policy classes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should evidence_refs be opaque ids or a signed manifest? (ops: prefer signed manifest for non-repudiation).
- Add schema versioning field to events (we need v1, v2 plan).
- Define exact retention buckets and chargeback model for customers who request >365d retention.
- Add cryptographic proof of operator identity (HSM-backed signatures) — feasibility follow-up with security.

Immediate next steps (who/what/when):
- Evan: implement basic event emitter in ops-sim and wire to staging-audit topic (ETA 2026-03-10).
- Liam: build validator and the CSV metrics exporter (ETA 2026-03-17).
- Asha: draft confluence spec for the evidence bundle format and append to linked artifacts (ETA 2026-03-05).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally pragmatic: we need something runnable for the SE/ops runbook before we harden the PRD. Don’t block on perfect cryptography — simulate with signed JSON blobs for the first pass.
- Comments inline are fine; I expect we'll iterate the schema after the first 3 sim runs.

Sample event excerpt (cut-and-paste friendly):
"event_id":"7f6e2b9a-0c3a-4f1b-9d21-6f2b9d11a123","timestamp_utc":"2026-02-25T18:22:33Z","actor_id":"cust:admin:acme-netops","actor_role":"customer_admin","action":"request_approval","resource":"customer/431/vpc/alpha/route-change/rt-77","outcome":"pending","evidence_refs":"eb-20260225-001","request_trace_id":"trace-20260225-004"

Unresolved: finalize the operator identity format and whether we push full evidence bundles to customer-managed S3 or store pointers only.

End of note.
